content.text:
You are the lead auditor for a read-only UI fidelity audit of the completed NIT-265 Neatlogs replica. The parent is the coordinator. You own the audit end to end and must return a consolidated report. The work is internally parallelizable AFTER evidence collection. Use your Task tool to split the three review areas among parallel internal subagents once evidence exists. Those reviewers must not use the browser.

## Repo and branch
Primary checkout: /Users/nitinkhanna/Desktop/tailor-neathack
A previous continuation found the NIT-265 worktree at /Users/nitinkhanna/.codex/worktrees/8dc3/tailor-neathack on branch codex/nit-265-replica-app at 1bee18f0cc631fbf5febb89e64346f4c80abfde4. VERIFY this. Do not trust it blindly.

Verify the current branch contains Codex’s latest NIT-265 implementation. Compare worktrees, branch tips, the handoff, and Linear. Preserve ALL existing work: do not reset, clean, checkout away uncommitted work, amend, force-push, merge, deploy, delete files, or discard the worktree. If the replica lives only in that worktree, audit there. Do not start NIT-269.

## Required reading before any browser or review work
1. /Users/nitinkhanna/Desktop/tailor-neathack/AGENTS.md and the same file in the NIT-265 worktree if it differs.
2. The project-local Entire skill. Find it in the repo (search for Entire skill / SKILL.md related to Entire recording). Follow its recording requirements for each supported agent session, including internal subagents. Report capture gaps honestly. Do not repair hooks, do not change .cursor/hooks.json or .entire/settings.json, do not skip hooks.
3. Linear issue NIT-265 (read-only). Use the Linear MCP namespace (plugin-linear-linear or user-Linear). Call GetDynamicTools for the tool schema before any Linear call. Do not modify Linear issues, comments, or status.
4. The existing handoff: docs/nit-265-cursor-handoff.md in the worktree that contains it, plus docs it points to that define replica scope (especially any fidelity or scope notes).

## Hard constraints
- AUDIT ONLY. Do not modify implementation, dependencies, configuration, package files, env files, hooks, or git state. The ONLY file you may create or edit is the audit report and its screenshot evidence directory (see below).
- Do not merge, deploy, push, commit, amend, or force-push.
- Do not add out-of-scope Neatlogs features just because they appear in the official UI. Record those as deliberate scope exclusions when NIT-265 / the handoff excludes them.
- Secrets: never print, log, commit, or screenshot NEATLOGS_API_KEY or any credential value. Do not read .env.local. A prior checkpoint contains a live API-key argument; do not copy it into the report or screenshots. npm run env:check only if you must know whether a key is set; it reports presence only.
- Official Neatlogs sandbox is READ-ONLY. Do not edit its data, settings, or either real project. Do not create, delete, or mutate traces, projects, API keys, or settings.
- Use the existing browser session (cursor-ide-browser MCP). Call GetDynamicTools for cursor-ide-browser before use. If login or access is missing, stop that part and mark it unverified. Ask the user for access in your final report; do not invent credentials or scrape tokens.
- YOU are the only browser user. Internal review subagents must not call browser tools, navigate, or open tabs. Do not run concurrent browser agents.
- Inspect the actual rendered UI. Do not rely on memory or documentation for visual claims. Documentation is for scope and expected behavior only.

## Browser evidence collection (you alone)
1. List existing browser tabs first. Reuse the authenticated official Neatlogs sandbox session. If several tabs exist, do not disrupt unrelated user tabs more than needed; lock only the tab you are driving.
2. Identify the local replica URL from the repo (dev server if already running; if none is running, you may start the existing replica dev server in the NIT-265 worktree ONLY if that does not change code or config). If you cannot run it without installs or config changes, mark local UI unverified and say why.
3. Capture PAIRED official-versus-local screenshots at matching viewport size, zoom, theme, and equivalent UI states for:
   - Layout / traces list: sidebar, header, table columns, spacing, typography, colours, borders, badges, icons, row density, scrolling, selected states.
   - Trace details: detail view, span hierarchy, timeline, inputs/outputs, errors, timing, tabs, expandable sections, long content, nested spans, and the default view.
   - Interaction and state: search, filters, sorting, navigation included in NIT-265; Back/Forward; direct links; reloads; empty results; loading/error states; repeated interactions. Confirm synthetic data stays consistent between list and detail.
4. For each pair record: reference URL (no secrets), capture time, viewport, zoom, theme, and UI state.
5. Use synthetic sandbox examples. Keep credentials and unrelated private information out of screenshots. Compare layout and behaviour, not identical trace text or timestamps.
6. Mark anything inaccessible as unverified. Do not guess.
7. Store screenshots under the NIT-265 worktree at docs/nit-265-ui-audit/ (create that evidence directory). Name files so pairs are obvious (e.g. list-official.png / list-local.png).

## Then split the review
After evidence is on disk, spawn three parallel internal generalPurpose subagents (run_in_background false so you wait for them, or background plus resume only if that is how your Task tool works — you must actually receive their findings before writing the final report). Give each the evidence directory, scope docs, and relevant code paths. They must NOT use the browser.

1. Layout and visual fidelity — official traces list vs replica. Sidebar, header, table columns, spacing, typography, colours, borders, badges, icons, row density, scrolling, selected states.
2. Trace details — detail view, span hierarchy, timeline, inputs/outputs, errors, timing, tabs, expandable sections, long content, nested spans, default view.
3. Interaction and state — search, filters, sorting, navigation in NIT-265 scope. Back/Forward, direct links, reloads, empty results, loading/error, repeated interactions, synthetic list/detail consistency.

Each reviewer returns: visual mismatches, functional defects, deliberate scope exclusions, unverified areas; affected screen; expected vs actual; reproduction steps; screenshot paths; relevant code locations; smallest suggested correction. They do not edit files.

## Final report
Write docs/NIT-265-ui-audit.md in the NIT-265 worktree (the replica branch). Do not commit it. Include:
- Short verdict on visual fidelity, limited to screens actually inspected.
- Prioritised findings: affected screen, expected vs actual, reproduction steps, screenshot evidence paths.
- Relevant code locations and the smallest suggested correction.
- Checklist of states inspected and gaps.
- Proposed parallel fix plan with non-overlapping file ownership.
- Separate sections or labels for visual mismatches, functional defects, deliberate scope exclusions, and unverified areas.
- Entire capture status for this lead session and each internal review session, including honest gaps (resolution, worktree, branch). Do not claim a capture you did not verify.
- Branch and commit you audited, and how you verified it is Codex’s latest implementation.

Do not start fixes. The user will review first.

## Return to the parent
A standalone summary:
1. Report path.
2. Branch, commit, worktree audited, and whether it is Codex’s latest.
3. Highest-impact findings only (severity, screen, expected vs actual), with screenshot paths.
4. Unverified gaps and any access you still need from the user.
5. Entire capture result and gaps.
6. Confirmation this pass did not modify implementation, dependencies, configuration, git history, Linear, or the official project, and did not merge or deploy.
I'll verify the NIT-265 worktree and required reading first, then collect paired screenshots myself before splitting the three reviews.

input.contents:
# NIT-265 UI fidelity audit

11 October 2026. Read-only. No implementation changes, and this report is not committed.

## Verdict

The public landing was compared with https://neatlogs.com/ in the same light, 100% browser capture. The headline and setup control line up. The hackathon strip, wordmark, and top navigation do not. A layout scrollbar also clips the local strip.

The authenticated Neatlogs traces list and trace detail were not compared. `app.neatlogs.com` opened the sign-in wall in this browser, so official app pixels are unverified. On the local replica, the two order-lookup fixtures stay consistent between list and detail, search and the latency filter behave as specified, and direct links work for the session that owns the browser cookie. The local list still hides its row count under the synthetic notice, the histogram bar sits on an unlabeled day, an applied filter does not look selected, and in-app Back adds a history entry so browser Back returns to the detail.

## What was audited

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Branch | `codex/nit-265-replica-app` |
| Commit | `1bee18f0cc631fbf5febb89e64346f4c80abfde4` |
| Subject | `docs: hand off NIT-265 replica for Cursor continuation` |
| Worktree | `/Users/nitinkhanna/.codex/worktrees/8dc3/tailor-neathack` |
| Base recorded by the handoff | `9ba9a45f6d8fa916a56bcee31738ba57cc7e2b99` |
| Ahead of local `origin/main` | 5 commits, and this tip is only on this branch |
| Remote feature branch | not present locally (`origin/codex/nit-265-replica-app` does not resolve) |
| Linear NIT-265 | still Todo, no comments, last updated 2026-10-11T02:06:16Z, before this tip |

Verification: `git rev-parse codex/nit-265-replica-app` is `1bee18f0cc631fbf5febb89e64346f4c80abfde4`. The log from `origin/main` is `64c3589`, `fa6f6d0`, `34f3aea`, `06d8a1d`, `1bee18f`. No other local ref contains `64c3589`. The handoff commit carries Entire checkpoint trailer `01M4N6EYWDZSBDYK5N9G2C7J10`. That trailer is historical Codex evidence, not this Cursor session.

The path named in the handoff was gone at the start of this audit: `/Users/nitinkhanna/.codex/worktrees/8dc3/` held only an empty marker file, and `git worktree list` did not include it. The branch itself was not checked out anywhere. This audit registered a worktree at that same path with `git worktree add` so the existing commit could be read and served. That did not move, reset, or change the branch tip. The dirty primary checkout on `main` (`0cc78ee`, modified `.gitignore`, untracked `.codex/`) was not switched or cleaned.

The local server is the existing `npm run dev` path: TypeScript from the primary checkout’s already-installed compiler, then `node src/server.ts` on `127.0.0.1:4321`. No `npm ci`, package, hook, or env change. `dist/` and `.local/` are gitignored build and fixture data. `git status` shows only untracked `docs/nit-265-ui-audit/` and this report.

## Capture conditions

Window: 2026-10-11 10:17–10:26 UTC. Theme: light. Zoom: 1. Reported device pixel ratio: 1. PNG size for every file below: 2688×1512.

Official landing CSS viewport after clearing emulation: 2688×1512. The local landing PNG was taken when the CSS layout viewport measured 2673×1512, which is the scrollbar mismatch below. Later local app pages used the natural viewport, about 2688×1512.

Evidence directory: `docs/nit-265-ui-audit/`.

| File | URL (no secrets) | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth-official.png` | `https://app.neatlogs.com/auth?intent=signin` with the sandbox traces callback | Sign-in wall |
| `landing-official.png` | `https://neatlogs.com/` | First screen |
| `landing-local.png` | `http://127.0.0.1:4321/` | First screen |
| `list-local.png` | `/demo/:id/traces` | Two fixture rows |
| `list-empty-local.png` | `?q=zz-no-fictional-trace` | No traces found |
| `list-latency-local.png` | `?minMs=45` | Exhausted row only |
| `detail-recovered-default-local.png` | recovered trace | Default, graph and timeline off |
| `detail-recovered-error-local.png` | same | `lookup_order_attempt_1` expanded |
| `detail-recovered-timeline-local.png` | same | Timeline on |
| `detail-recovered-graph-local.png` | same | Graph and timeline on |
| `detail-recovered-graph-select-local.png` | same | Failed span highlighted in graph and timeline |
| `detail-exhausted-default-local.png` | exhausted trace | Default |
| `detail-span-link-local.png` | `?span=…-exhausted-attempt-2` | That span expanded |
| `detail-direct-link-error-local.png` | older session’s trace URL | Cookie no longer owns that session |
| `detail-unknown-trace-local.png` | `…/traces/missing-trace` | Trace not found |
| `detail-unavailable-toast-local.png` | same bytes as the span-link shot | Toast not visible |

## Visual mismatches

### Landing, compared with the live public site

1. **Scrollbar and a narrower page.** Official strip reaches the window edge. Local shows a classic scrollbar, and the strip’s right edge is page background. The footer is `position:absolute; top:100vh`, so the page scrolls, while `scrollbar-width:none` is set on `.landing` and `body:has(.landing)` but not on `html`. Screenshots: `landing-official.png`, `landing-local.png`. Smallest correction in `public/style.css`: stop the footer from growing scroll height, and hide the scrollbar on `html` as well.

2. **Hackathon strip.** Both images read `Oct 10–12` and `$19,000`. Official is a 32px strip, fill about `(2,141,194)`, with the date in a rounded outline. Local is 31px `#008db3` with the date as plain text. Code: `landing()` in `src/client.ts`, `.hack` in `public/style.css`. Smallest correction: 32px, `#028dc2`, and a chip around the date only.

3. **Wordmark.** Official is a compact mark starting further left. Local uses generic monospace at 30px with `letter-spacing:-1.3px` and `padding:12px 3vw`, so the mark is wider and further right. Geist Mono is already loaded for the setup control. Smallest correction: use that face for `.public-nav .wordmark` and reduce the nav’s horizontal padding.

4. **Nav chrome.** Official Manifesto is a pale cyan pill with a cyan dot. Product has a chevron, Docs has an arrow, and a rule sits before the black button. Local is flat text plus the black pill. Code: the `public-nav` buttons in `landing()`. Smallest correction: draw the chip, arrows, and divider. Leave those destinations non-navigating.

The headline boxes match (about 1169px wide, tops one pixel apart). The setup control’s label, agent marks, copy chip, and cyan edge match in these stills. Motion was not compared.

### Local traces list (no official list pixels)

5. **Synthetic notice covers the pager.** `1 – 2 of 2` and the page chip sit under the fixed notice at the bottom right. Same on the empty and latency lists. Code: `.demo-notice{position:fixed;bottom:4px;right:12px;z-index:3}` in `public/style.css`; the count is in `list()` in `src/client.ts`. Screenshots: `list-local.png`, `list-latency-local.png`, `list-empty-local.png`. Smallest correction: move the notice above the pagination row.

6. **Applied latency filter looks idle.** `?minMs=45` changes the capsule text to `Latency ≥ 45ms` and keeps the same white capsule as the unused filters. Code: `list()` changes the summary text; selected styling exists for `.filter-popover[open] summary` only. Screenshots: `list-local.png`, `list-latency-local.png`. Smallest correction: when `minMs`, `scenario`, `detection`, or `tag` is set, give that summary the open-state fill.

7. **Histogram bar does not name its day or scale with count.** Both rows are 11:47 PM Oct 10. The accessible name says the filtered traces are on Oct 10. The gray block is the unlabeled cell immediately before the Oct 11 tick (index 12, label `''`). The 2-row list and the 1-row list paint the same full-height `#97979f` block. The empty search correctly draws no block. Code: `i===12&&data.filtered` and `.day.populated{background:#97979f}` with no height scale. Screenshots: the three list shots. Smallest correction: label index 12 `Oct 10`, and set the block height from `data.filtered`.

### Local trace detail (no official detail pixels)

8. **One step, two duration units.** `prepare_order_answer` and `prepare_escalation` are `370µs` in the step row and `0.37 ms` on the timeline. The step row multiplies values under 1ms by 1000 and appends `µs`; the timeline always prints `ms`. Fixture value is `0.37`. Screenshot: `detail-recovered-timeline-local.png`. Smallest correction: one duration helper for the step row, timeline label, and attributes list in `src/client.ts`.

9. **Graph kind icons.** Guardrail and chain nodes use the tool icon in the graph. The step list uses the tree icon unless the span is a tool or an error. Error nodes correctly use the X. Screenshot: `detail-recovered-graph-local.png`. Smallest correction: use the step-row icon choice for graph children.

10. **Execution Failed pills can leave the card.** At 2688px they sit in the gutter and clear the rail. `.span-detection` is `position:absolute; right:calc(100% + 45px)`, and the card is 704px and centered, so just above the 900px breakpoint the pills can enter the 66px rail. Screenshots of the wide state: `detail-exhausted-default-local.png`, `detail-span-link-local.png`. Smallest correction: keep the pill inside the row, or use the static placement from about 1100px down.

## Functional defects

11. **In-app Back pushes history.** From the exhausted trace opened via `?minMs=45`, the in-app back control returns to that filtered list, because `returnTo` remembers the list URL. `navigate()` always `history.pushState`s, so browser Back then restores the detail, and Forward restores `?minMs=45`. A reload of the detail page clears `returnTo`, so the next in-app Back drops `minMs`. A reload of the list URL keeps the filter, because `render()` rereads `location.search`. Code: `returnTo`, `navigate()`, and the `data-nav` click handler in `src/client.ts`. Smallest correction: if `.back-link` has a `returnTo`, call `history.back()`; use `navigate(base)` only when detail was opened directly.

12. **Ingested time and the detection count are literals.** Every row prints `11:47 PM` / `Oct 10` instead of formatting `ingestedAt` (`2026-10-10T18:17:00.000Z`). That string is right in UTC+5:30 and wrong in other zones. The detection cell prints `Execution Failed 2` whenever any span has `detection`. The exhausted fixture does have two detected errors, so these shots are numerically right. Code: `list()` in `src/client.ts`. Smallest correction: format `t.ingestedAt`, and count spans with `detection`.

13. **Expand all repeats the root.** No screenshot; the control is on every detail view. The handler adds every span id, including the root, whose input and output are already outside the card. Smallest correction: add only spans with a `parentId`.

The older-session URL in `detail-direct-link-error-local.png` is not a routing bug. A second local session was created in this browser at 2026-10-11T10:20:40Z. `POST /api/sessions` replaces the HttpOnly cookie (`src/server.ts`), and `authorize()` rejects any other id (`src/store.ts`). After opening the cookie’s own session, direct trace URLs, reload, and `?span=` worked. `missing-trace` returns `NOT_FOUND: Trace not found in this session` (`detail-unknown-trace-local.png`).

## Deliberate scope exclusions

From NIT-265, `docs/nit-265-reference.md`, and the handoff. These are not defects.

- Hero and nav CTA say “Try with your project” instead of “Start free”. Marketing links toast and do not navigate. Below-the-fold marketing is absent.
- Two synthetic order lookups, not the sandbox’s 10-trace catalogue. Saved project text does not choose the fixture.
- Evals and Comments stay empty. Replay, Sessions, Users, date, metadata, and advanced filters are unavailable controls. Search is a case-insensitive substring, without span chips.
- Column headers are not buttons. Sorting was not part of this slice.
- Graph is a fixed pane. The navigator is a two-trace picker. Timeline labels include durations. Search, replay, comments, and Ask neat AI on the detail header do not run those products.
- Header duration comes from the same root record (43ms recovered, 51ms exhausted), so the reference’s 50ms-versus-51ms header split is avoided on purpose.
- Analytics, full auth, billing, assistant, and NIT-269 were not started.

## Unverified

- Official traces list, trace detail, graph, timeline, badges, row selection, and histogram. `auth-official.png` is only the sign-in wall. Sign in to the existing Tailor Demo Sandbox in this browser, read-only, to capture those pairs.
- Ask neat AI toast. `detail-unavailable-toast-local.png` is byte-identical to `detail-span-link-local.png` (sha1 `b8426847c1d8e7f73b805420a361fa2847545910`) and shows no toast. The handler and the 4.5s bottom-center `.toast` rule exist, so a late check would also find nothing. Recapture within that window.
- Loading. `render()` shows “Loading synthetic traces…” and some navigations returned a blank snapshot. No loading screenshot.
- Workflow, Detections, and Tags applied in the UI. The server filters exist; this pass did not screenshot them.
- Setup-button motion, dark theme, 390px, persistent backend failure, and a pixel-level hero-photograph diff. The layout review treated the silver scene as matching at headline scale.
- Whether official graph selection also highlights the step row. Locally it highlights the node and the timeline row only and does not change the URL.

## States inspected

| State | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Public landing, official and local | Inspected |
| Authenticated traces list and detail | Blocked at sign-in |
| Local list, two fixtures | Inspected |
| Empty search `zz-no-fictional-trace` | Inspected |
| Latency `minMs=45` | One exhausted row |
| Recovered default, error expand, timeline, graph, graph select | Inspected |
| Exhausted default | Inspected |
| Direct `?span=` | Expands that span |
| In-app Back, browser Back, browser Forward | Filter restored, then history returns to detail |
| Reload of `?minMs=45` | Filter kept |
| Direct URL for a session the cookie does not own | Honest not-found |
| Unknown trace id | Honest not-found |
| Unavailable toast, loading, date/session/user/eval editors, dark theme, mobile | Not captured |

List and detail agree. Recovered: no detection, 43ms root, outcome `order_found`, order `SYN-ORDER-103`, one ERROR child. Exhausted: Execution Failed twice, 51ms root, escalation text that says no ticket was sent, two ERROR children.

## Parallel fix plan

Do not start until review. Three owners, no shared files. Class names below are the contract between owners.

| Owner | File | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Landing and list chrome | `public/style.css` | Footer scroll and `html` scrollbar; 32px `#028dc2` strip; Geist Mono wordmark and nav padding; Manifesto chip, chevrons, and divider using classes `nav-current`, `nav-caret`, `nav-rule`; move `.demo-notice` above the pager; `.is-selected` fill for an applied capsule; histogram block height from a `--count` custom property; keep `.span-detection` inside the row |
| List and detail behavior | `src/client.ts` | Date chip markup; those nav classes; format `ingestedAt`; count detections; label Oct 10 and set `--count`; add `is-selected` when a filter value is set; one duration helper; graph icons match the step row; Expand all skips the root; `.back-link` uses `history.back()` when `returnTo` is set |
| Fixture contract | `src/fixtures.ts` | No visual change. Re-read only if a duration helper needs the stored `0.37` to stay the single source |

`public/assets/setup-prompt.css`, `src/server.ts`, and `src/store.ts` stay untouched for this pass.

## Entire capture

Skill used: `.agents/skills/entire-continuity/SKILL.md` on this commit. The primary checkout’s `AGENTS.md` does not mention that skill; the replica checkout’s copy does. `entire doctor` and `entire status` were not run, because this pass was observation-only. Hooks were not edited. Entire CLI is 0.11.4.

| Session | Resolution | Status | Worktree and branch | Live capture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lead Cursor session `4a4e0ead-edae-4d72-9c11-9cf47062fc8b` | `caller-ambiguous` | `idle` | Primary `/Users/nitinkhanna/Desktop/tailor-neathack`, `main` | Unverified. Not `caller-env` or `ancestry`. `last_active` stayed `2026-10-11T15:40:49+05:30` through the later audit. The CLI also said several sessions claimed the command and none could be ordered |
| Layout review `2cc61e4c-f3fb-450b-8034-5c322b3e1c1f` | `caller-ambiguous` | `idle` | Same primary `main` | Unverified |
| Detail review `720becc4-44df-4922-a8ed-1dc1914903fc` | `caller-ambiguous` | `idle` | Same primary `main` | Unverified |
| Interaction review `78a79fe8-9826-4489-81f3-040639930d4b` | `caller-ambiguous` | `idle` | Same primary `main` | Unverified |
